forks.decision: External tasks run fully native with a local checkout without upstream history, a local uv venv or Go/Rust toolchain, and our replay of the instance's FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS tests; no Docker

contradictions: Contract > Admission (spec L70) and AC-4: a cached verdict is returned 'without starting any subprocess' when its key matches, but the key includes the env fingerprint, which Contract > Identity (L59) defines over toolchain versions (uv and Python, go, rustc and cargo). In a fresh process, such as c3's `run.py --panel` calling admit (bench-panel-manifest.md L53) or run.py's refusal check (L71), computing the current fingerprint needs `go version`, `rustc --version`, or `uv --version` subprocesses. test_cached_verdict_is_read_without_rerun checks only a second in-process call. Cook will therefore either violate the claim or match on a memoized or skipped fingerprint, which defeats the drift check. The likely intent is 'without re-running the round trip'.

Contract > Preflight CLI (L72) and Interface sketches (L109) define `python3 benchmark/external/preflight.py` with no arguments. The parent Quality gates (benchmark-gepa-overhaul.md:179) run `python3 benchmark/external/preflight.py --panel benchmark/panels/<name>.json` and expect a gold, empty, and tampered report for every admitted task. The parent gate cannot run against the CLI this child specifies.

Contract > Contamination (L76) and Non-goals (L138) say `analyze.py` excludes contaminated rows for panel runs and assign that to consumers, but no sibling owns it. bench-panel-manifest Non-goals (L116) defers contamination to c2. bench-model-judge's analyze Applicability Label x Mode table (L68, AC-5) computes correctness over every row with no contamination filter. bench-evolution-loop applies the rule only inside evolve (L46-47). Panel-run analyze reports will count grader-correct contaminated rows as correct, against the seam this child states.
unsupported_assumptions: Contract > Admission (L68), AC-4, and Fixtures (L79) refuse 'rows that lack a level or hardware field (unclassified)'. This assumes dataset rows carry level and hardware fields, and they do not. FeatureBench Lite at HF tag v1.1 (data/lite-00000-of-00001.parquet) has only the row keys instance_id, patch, test_patch, FAIL_TO_PASS, PASS_TO_PASS, image_name, repo, base_commit, problem_statement, and repo_settings. The level appears only as the instance_id suffix `.lv1` or `.lv2`. The only hardware hint is repo_settings.docker_specs.run_args.cuda_visible_devices, and it is set to '6,7' on CPU-only Pareto-12 rows: seaborn x2, sympy, xarray, sphinx, and pandas. SWE-bench Multilingual rows at 846e647b have neither field. A literal implementation refuses every real instance as unclassified or GPU-flagged, so featurebench_admitted, go_admitted, and rust_admitted are all 0, while the synthetic fixture, which ships level and hardware fields, passes every test. The refusal happens before the round trip, so the admission round trip does not guard this.

Contract > Native grading (L64-65) and AC-3 assume FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS entries are per-test IDs: 'parses per-test verdicts', 'a listed test missing from the output counts as failed', and pass_rate over listed tests. In FeatureBench v1.1 Lite rows the entries are test file paths. The sympy test_nullspace row has FAIL_TO_PASS ['sympy/polys/matrices/tests/test_nullspace.py'], and the seaborn test_regression row has PASS_TO_PASS ['tests/_marks/test_bar.py', 'tests/test_algorithms.py', ...]. pytest -rA prints `path::test` node IDs, so exact per-test matching marks every FeatureBench entry missing, gold never resolves, and no FeatureBench task is admitted. The claim is not marked [speculating], the spec gives no file-level aggregation rule, and the only parser test (test_go_and_rust_outputs_parse_per_test) covers Go and Rust only.
acceptance_gaps: AC-5 and Contract > Preflight CLI (L72) require a nonzero exit 'naming the empty family when any of them is 0'. test_zero_featurebench_admitted_reports_and_fails covers only featurebench_admitted 0, and test_preflight_cli_reports_admitted covers only the all-admitted case. No test has go_admitted or rust_admitted at 0 with both primary and fallback refused, so a CLI that checks only FeatureBench passes every listed test.

AC-5 says that when `run.py --tasks` names an admitted instance ID THE SYSTEM SHALL plan it. test_tasks_flag_resolves_admitted_ids checks only that the ID is not rejected and that `--tasks all` plans no external cell. Nothing checks that the ExternalTask is loaded and registered in TASKS, which run_single and _run_single_in_repo index (benchmark/run.py:479,518 at HEAD), or that the runner is invoked through prepare. An implementation that accepts the ID and then raises KeyError into an error row passes.

AC-2 and Contract > Identity (L59) say the external task digest covers the gold patch, test patch, FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS lists, base_commit, and data revision. Among row inputs, test_env_and_instance_change_run_key varies only the held-out test patch. An implementation that leaves the gold patch, the test lists, base_commit, or the data revision out of the digest passes, and stored rows would then be reused across a changed instance.
